name: Incline Lever Machine Alternating Press
description: A machine incline chest press performed in an alternating arm pattern rather than simultaneously. Each arm presses independently while the other holds the contracted or extended position. The alternating pattern creates greater focus on each side individually, allows detection of left-right strength imbalances, and increases the total time under tension per set compared to bilateral pressing.

execution.starting_position: Sit in an incline chest press machine. Grip both handles with an overhand grip. Adjust the seat height so the handles are at upper chest level. Begin with both arms in the loaded (retracted) position.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the seat height so the handles align with the upper chest/clavicle. Select a moderate weight appropriate for single-arm pressing (lighter than bilateral weight).
steps: Step 1: Begin with both arms loaded at the chest. Press the right arm to full extension.
Step 2: Hold the right arm extended. Begin pressing the left arm to full extension.
Step 3: Return the right arm to the loaded position as the left arm finishes its extension.
Step 4: Alternate: right press → left press → right return → left return. Each full alternating cycle is one rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as each arm presses, inhale as it returns. Breathing rhythm may need to be adapted to the alternating cadence.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to assist the pressing arm — keep shoulders square
Resting at the loaded position rather than maintaining active tension
Pressing too fast to maintain control of the alternating pattern
safety_considerations: Machine provides a fixed path — ensure seat height is correct before beginning
If the machine does not allow true alternating independent arms, perform standard bilateral pressing instead
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension on each arm, fully loaded at the bottom. Each arm completes a full range per alternation.
coaching_cues: Press one side, hold the other — do not let the resting arm drop completely
Keep shoulders square — the alternating load tries to rotate you
